title: Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators fan out in Uttar Pradesh
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumer' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.
gs_connection: GS-3 Indian Economy: Macroeconomic Stability, Banking, Fiscal Policy & Trade

mcqs.q:
With reference to macroeconomic dynamics linked to "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators fan out in Uttar Pradesh", consider the following statements:
1. An increase in the policy Repo Rate by the RBI typically leads to an appreciation of the domestic currency in the short run.
2. Headline Inflation measured by CPI includes food and energy components, whereas Core Inflation excludes them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. A rate hike attracts capital inflows seeking higher yields, putting upward pressure on the rupee. Core inflation strips out volatile food and fuel prices.

mcqs.q:
Which of the following measures is/are likely to reduce the Current Account Deficit (CAD) of India?
1. Imposing higher import duties on non-essential luxury items
2. Devaluation of the domestic currency to boost export competitiveness
3. Increasing incentives under Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.explanation: All three measures help compress CAD: restricting non-essential imports reduces outflow, a weaker currency makes exports cheaper globally, and domestic production replaces imports.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):
1. It consists of six members: three from the RBI and three appointed by the Central Government.
2. The Governor of the RBI possesses a casting vote in case of a tie.
3. The inflation target of 4% (+/- 2%) is determined by the MPC itself without Government consultation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act. Statement 3 is incorrect because the inflation target is determined by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI once every 5 years.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

mcqs.q:
With reference to public finance and macroeconomic considerations impacting "Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators", consider the following statements:
1. Capital expenditure creates tangible physical assets or reduces financial liabilities, whereas revenue expenditure does not create any permanent asset.
2. Grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to States for creation of capital assets are classified as Capital Expenditure in the Union Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Capital expenditure leads to asset creation or liability reduction. Statement 2 is incorrect: Grants-in-aid given to States, even if utilized for capital asset creation, are accounting-wise classified as Revenue Expenditure in the Union Budget, though highlighted as 'Effective Capital Expenditure' in budget analyses.

mcqs.q:
In the context of recent developments concerning "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi - www.pib.gov.in", consider the following statements regarding the relevant constitutional mechanisms:
1. The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 cannot be curtailed by an ordinary statute.
2. Delegated legislation made by the executive is subject to judicial review on grounds of exceeding legislative competence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Article 32 is part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution and cannot be abrogated by ordinary law. Subordinate or delegated legislation must conform strictly to the parent statute and constitutional limits.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding statutory vs constitutional bodies in India:
1. A constitutional body derives its authority directly from an Article of the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are legally binding on the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because recommendations of the Finance Commission under Article 280 are advisory in nature, though conventionally accepted by the Government.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the doctrine of "Separation of Powers" in the Indian Constitutional scheme, which one of the following is correct?
(a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
options: (a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
mcqs.explanation: Option (b) is correct. Article 50 (DPSP) directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services. The Indian Constitution adopts a system of checks and balances rather than strict water-tight separation.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

mcqs.q:
With reference to public finance and macroeconomic considerations impacting "Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah ad", consider the following statements:
1. Capital expenditure creates tangible physical assets or reduces financial liabilities, whereas revenue expenditure does not create any permanent asset.
2. Grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to States for creation of capital assets are classified as Capital Expenditure in the Union Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Capital expenditure leads to asset creation or liability reduction. Statement 2 is incorrect: Grants-in-aid given to States, even if utilized for capital asset creation, are accounting-wise classified as Revenue Expenditure in the Union Budget, though highlighted as 'Effective Capital Expenditure' in budget analyses.

title: Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches in Various Parts of the Country - www.pib.gov.in
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

mcqs.q:
In the context of recent developments concerning "Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches in Various Parts of the Country - www.pib.gov.in", consider the following statements regarding the relevant constitutional mechanisms:
1. The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 cannot be curtailed by an ordinary statute.
2. Delegated legislation made by the executive is subject to judicial review on grounds of exceeding legislative competence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Article 32 is part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution and cannot be abrogated by ordinary law. Subordinate or delegated legislation must conform strictly to the parent statute and constitutional limits.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding statutory vs constitutional bodies in India:
1. A constitutional body derives its authority directly from an Article of the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are legally binding on the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because recommendations of the Finance Commission under Article 280 are advisory in nature, though conventionally accepted by the Government.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the doctrine of "Separation of Powers" in the Indian Constitutional scheme, which one of the following is correct?
(a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
options: (a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
mcqs.explanation: Option (b) is correct. Article 50 (DPSP) directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services. The Indian Constitution adopts a system of checks and balances rather than strict water-tight separation.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches i", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches i", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches i", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Recommendation Regarding Establishment of Supreme Court Benches i", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

title: Debates on Judgements of Supreme Court in Parliament - www.pib.gov.in
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

title: The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but is the banking system ready for it?
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.
gs_connection: GS-3 Indian Economy: Macroeconomic Stability, Banking, Fiscal Policy & Trade

mcqs.q:
With reference to macroeconomic dynamics linked to "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but is the banking system ready for it?", consider the following statements:
1. An increase in the policy Repo Rate by the RBI typically leads to an appreciation of the domestic currency in the short run.
2. Headline Inflation measured by CPI includes food and energy components, whereas Core Inflation excludes them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. A rate hike attracts capital inflows seeking higher yields, putting upward pressure on the rupee. Core inflation strips out volatile food and fuel prices.

mcqs.q:
Which of the following measures is/are likely to reduce the Current Account Deficit (CAD) of India?
1. Imposing higher import duties on non-essential luxury items
2. Devaluation of the domestic currency to boost export competitiveness
3. Increasing incentives under Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.explanation: All three measures help compress CAD: restricting non-essential imports reduces outflow, a weaker currency makes exports cheaper globally, and domestic production replaces imports.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):
1. It consists of six members: three from the RBI and three appointed by the Central Government.
2. The Governor of the RBI possesses a casting vote in case of a tie.
3. The inflation target of 4% (+/- 2%) is determined by the MPC itself without Government consultation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act. Statement 3 is incorrect because the inflation target is determined by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI once every 5 years.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

mcqs.q:
With reference to public finance and macroeconomic considerations impacting "The expected credit loss framework is a necessary evolution—but i", consider the following statements:
1. Capital expenditure creates tangible physical assets or reduces financial liabilities, whereas revenue expenditure does not create any permanent asset.
2. Grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to States for creation of capital assets are classified as Capital Expenditure in the Union Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Capital expenditure leads to asset creation or liability reduction. Statement 2 is incorrect: Grants-in-aid given to States, even if utilized for capital asset creation, are accounting-wise classified as Revenue Expenditure in the Union Budget, though highlighted as 'Effective Capital Expenditure' in budget analyses.

title: Hospital chains weigh drug price cap impact as Supreme Court scrutiny looms
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

six_point_gist.1_genesis: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.
six_point_gist.2_constitutional_statutory: Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). six_point_gist.3_nodal_authorities: Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.
six_point_gist.4_data_rankings: Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.
six_point_gist.5_bottlenecks_challenges: Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.
six_point_gist.6_roadmap_prelims_anchor: Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

title: ₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra wants banks to rethink big-ticket loans
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.

mcqs.q:
In the context of recent developments concerning "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra wants banks to rethink big-ticket loans", consider the following statements regarding the relevant constitutional mechanisms:
1. The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 cannot be curtailed by an ordinary statute.
2. Delegated legislation made by the executive is subject to judicial review on grounds of exceeding legislative competence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Article 32 is part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution and cannot be abrogated by ordinary law. Subordinate or delegated legislation must conform strictly to the parent statute and constitutional limits.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding statutory vs constitutional bodies in India:
1. A constitutional body derives its authority directly from an Article of the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are legally binding on the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because recommendations of the Finance Commission under Article 280 are advisory in nature, though conventionally accepted by the Government.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the doctrine of "Separation of Powers" in the Indian Constitutional scheme, which one of the following is correct?
(a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
options: (a) It is explicitly declared in Part III of the Constitution as a Fundamental Right.
(b) Article 50 of Directive Principles directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
(c) The Indian Constitution enforces a strict water-tight division of powers identical to the US Constitution.
(d) The President of India is an integral part of Parliament, which violates the basic structure.
mcqs.explanation: Option (b) is correct. Article 50 (DPSP) directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services. The Indian Constitution adopts a system of checks and balances rather than strict water-tight separation.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

mcqs.q:
With reference to public finance and macroeconomic considerations impacting "₹1,000 crore to one firm vs small businesses: Why RBI Governor Sa", consider the following statements:
1. Capital expenditure creates tangible physical assets or reduces financial liabilities, whereas revenue expenditure does not create any permanent asset.
2. Grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to States for creation of capital assets are classified as Capital Expenditure in the Union Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Capital expenditure leads to asset creation or liability reduction. Statement 2 is incorrect: Grants-in-aid given to States, even if utilized for capital asset creation, are accounting-wise classified as Revenue Expenditure in the Union Budget, though highlighted as 'Effective Capital Expenditure' in budget analyses.

six_point_gist.1_genesis: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.
six_point_gist.2_constitutional_statutory: Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.
six_point_gist.3_nodal_authorities: Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).
six_point_gist.4_data_rankings: Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.
six_point_gist.5_bottlenecks_challenges: Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.
six_point_gist.6_roadmap_prelims_anchor: Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.

prelims_fact_box: MPC Composition: 6 members; Governor has casting vote; external members hold office for 4 years and are NOT eligible for re-appointment.
SDF mechanism: Introduced under Section 17 of RBI Act 1934 as an uncollateralized liquidity absorption tool.
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR): Maintained under Section 24 of Banking Regulation Act 1949 in gold, cash, or approved government securities.
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR): Maintained under Section 42 of RBI Act 1934 exclusively with RBI in cash.
digestible_fact_sheet.trap_alert: UPSC Trap Alert: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) allows the RBI to absorb overnight liquidity from commercial banks WITHOUT offering government securities as collateral, unlike the Reverse Repo facility which requires collateral.

title: Supreme Court Ruling on Governor's Assent to State Bills under Article 200
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the Governor's powers regarding Bills passed by the State Legislature under Article 200 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor may declare that he assents to the Bill, or that he withholds assent therefrom, or that he reserves the Bill for the consideration of the President.
2. The Constitution specifies a strict time limit of six weeks within which the Governor must return a Bill for reconsideration.
3. If a Money Bill is returned by the Governor and passed again by the Legislature, the Governor cannot withhold assent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct (Article 200). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constitution uses the phrase 'as soon as possible' and DOES NOT specify a numerical deadline. Statement 3 is incorrect because a Governor CANNOT return a Money Bill for reconsideration in the first place.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reservation of State Bills for the President's consideration under Article 201:
1. When a Bill is reserved by a Governor for the President, the President must declare assent within 6 months.
2. The President may direct the Governor to return the Bill (unless it is a Money Bill) to the State Legislature.
3. If the State Legislature passes the Bill again within six months, it is obligatory for the President to give his assent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect (no constitutional time limit on President). Statement 2 is correct (Article 201 proviso). Statement 3 is incorrect: Unlike the Governor, the President is NOT obligated to give assent even if the State Legislature repasses the bill.

1. Administrative Reforms Commission (1969)

mcqs.explanation: Both Sarkaria Commission (1988) and Punchhi Commission (2010) explicitly recommended mandatory consultation with the State Chief Minister during the appointment of the Governor to prevent partisan appointments.

mcqs.q:
Under Article 163 of the Constitution, the Governor is aided and advised by the Council of Ministers except in matters where he is required to act in his discretion. In this context, consider the following:
1. If any question arises whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion or not, the decision of the Governor in his discretion shall be final.
2. The validity of anything done by the Governor cannot be called in question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion.
3. The advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor can be inquired into by the High Court under Article 226.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are direct provisions of Article 163(2). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 163(3) expressly bars all courts from inquiring into what advice was tendered by Ministers to the Governor.

title: Delimitation Commission & Post-2026 Lok Sabha Seat Freeze Reassessment
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Rapid technological convergence in deep tech, indigenization under the National Deep Tech Startup Policy, space sector commercialization through IN-SPACe, and frontier bio-manufacturing under the BioE3 policy.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 51A(h) directs every citizen to develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry. Governed administratively by the Indian Space Policy 2023, IT Act 2000, and National Quantum Mission guidelines.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Department of Space (ISRO, IN-SPACe, NewSpace India Limited - NSIL), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and Department of Science and Technology (DST).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: India's R&D expenditure stands at approximately 0.65% of GDP, with targets to increase to 2%. National Quantum Mission was approved with an outlay of ₹6,003 crore over 8 years (2023-2031).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: High import reliance on advanced semiconductor fabrication (sub-7nm), intellectual property licensing bottlenecks, private sector R&D expenditure deficits, and cross-border data transfer compliance under DPDP Act 2023.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Commercialization through NSIL (commercial arm of ISRO) and IN-SPACe (single-window nodal agency for non-government private entities), Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act 2023 mobilizing ₹50,000 crore for university research.
gs_connection: Links to GS-2 Representation of People, Delimitation (Article 82 & 170), Federalism, Demographic Transition, and Constitutional Amendments (42nd, 84th, 87th).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Delimitation Commission in India:
1. The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the President of India and works in collaboration with the Election Commission of India.
2. The orders issued by the Delimitation Commission can be challenged in the Supreme Court on grounds of constitutional violation.
3. When the orders of the Delimitation Commission are laid before the Lok Sabha, the House can modify or reject them by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect: Under Article 329(a) and the Delimitation Act, the orders of the Commission have the full force of law, CANNOT be called in question in any court, and CANNOT be modified by Parliament or state legislatures.

mcqs.q:
The freeze on the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha as per the 1971 Census was first effected by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
(a) 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
(b) 44th Amendment Act, 1978
(c) 84th Amendment Act, 2001
(d) 91st Amendment Act, 2003
mcqs.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) first froze the total number of seats in Lok Sabha and Assemblies until the year 2000 based on the 1971 census. The 84th Amendment Act (2001) extended this freeze for another 25 years until after 2026.

mcqs.q:
Under the 87th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, the internal delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies (without changing the total number of seats) was permitted on the basis of which Census?
(a) 1971 Census
(b) 1981 Census
(c) 1991 Census
(d) 2001 Census
mcqs.explanation: The 84th Amendment initially allowed internal delimitation based on the 1991 census, but the 87th Amendment Act of 2003 substituted the 2001 census for internal constituency adjustments.

mcqs.q:
Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates the readjustment of allocation of seats to the states in the Lok Sabha after each Census by such authority as Parliament may by law provide?
(a) Article 80
(b) Article 81
(c) Article 82
(d) Article 83
mcqs.explanation: Article 82 provides for the readjustment of seats and boundaries after each census through an enactment of a Delimitation Act by Parliament.

title: Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Information (Art 19(1)(a))
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.
gs_connection: Links to GS-2 Indian Polity: Fundamental Rights (Art 19(1)(a) Free Speech & Right to Know), Electoral Reforms, Representation of the People Act 1951 (Section 29C), and Judicial Review.

mcqs.q:
In Association for Democratic Reforms (2024), the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bonds Scheme primarily on the grounds of violating which Fundamental Right?
(a) Article 14 (Equality before Law)
(b) Article 19(1)(a) (Freedom of Speech and Expression, including Right to Information)
(c) Article 21 (Right to Personal Liberty)
(d) Article 25 (Freedom of Conscience)
options: (b) Article 19(1)(a) (Freedom of Speech and Expression, including Right to Information)
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court held that the voter's right to know about candidates and the financial sources backing political parties is an integral facet of Article 19(1)(a) required for meaningful exercise of the franchise.

mcqs.q:
Prior to the 2017 amendments, Section 182 of the Companies Act, 2013 capped a company's political contributions at what percentage of its average net profits during the three immediately preceding financial years?
(a) 5%
(b) 7.5%
(c) 10%
(d) 15%
mcqs.explanation: Before the Finance Act 2017 removed the cap, companies could only donate up to 7.5% of their average net profits over the prior three financial years. The Supreme Court struck down the unlimited corporate funding amendment.

mcqs.q:
Under Section 29C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, political parties are required to declare donations exceeding what threshold amount to the Election Commission of India?
(a) ₹2,000
(b) ₹10,000
(c) ₹20,000
(d) ₹50,000
mcqs.explanation: Under Section 29C of the RPA 1951, the treasurer of every political party must submit an annual report to the ECI detailing all contributions received from individuals and companies exceeding ₹20,000.

mcqs.q:
Which committee on electoral reforms recommended that there should be complete state funding of elections in kind (facilities and airtime) rather than cash subsidies?
(a) Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)
(b) Tarkunde Committee (1975)
(c) Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990)
(d) Santhanam Committee (1964)
mcqs.explanation: The Indrajit Gupta Committee on State Funding of Elections (1998) endorsed partial state funding in kind (paper, fuel, transport, airtime on state media) for recognized political parties to create a level playing field.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Inform", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Inform", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Inform", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Inform", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Supreme Court Verdict on Electoral Bonds Scheme & Right to Inform":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

title: Sub-classification of Scheduled Castes & Creamy Layer: 7-Judge Bench Verdict
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'Sub-classification of Scheduled Castes & Creamy Layer: 7-Jud' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.

title: Simultaneous Elections: High-Level Committee on 'One Nation, One Election'
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The integrity of the electoral process and anti-defection provisions have come under heightened scrutiny due to delays by legislative Speakers in deciding disqualification petitions and debates over simultaneous elections.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 324 (Superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in ECI), Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law added by 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985), and Articles 102(2) & 191(2).

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Election Commission of India (ECI), Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act 2023, and Presiding Officers of Parliament and State Assemblies.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act 2003 deleted the split provision (1/3rd members), requiring a merger of at least 2/3rds of elected members to escape disqualification under paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: The partisan role of the Speaker, indefinite pendency of disqualification proceedings, and judicial review timing: in Kihoto Hollohan (1992), the SC held that judicial review is impermissible before the Speaker passes an order, except under grave interim circumstances.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) ruled that Speakers must decide disqualification petitions within a reasonable period, usually 3 months. Law Commission and Dinesh Goswami Committee recommend vesting the power of disqualification in the Governor/President acting on the binding advice of the Election Commission.

title: Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions of Service) Act
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The integrity of the electoral process and anti-defection provisions have come under heightened scrutiny due to delays by legislative Speakers in deciding disqualification petitions and debates over simultaneous elections.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 324 (Superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in ECI), Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law added by 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985), and Articles 102(2) & 191(2).

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Election Commission of India (ECI), Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act 2023, and Presiding Officers of Parliament and State Assemblies.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act 2003 deleted the split provision (1/3rd members), requiring a merger of at least 2/3rds of elected members to escape disqualification under paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: The partisan role of the Speaker, indefinite pendency of disqualification proceedings, and judicial review timing: in Kihoto Hollohan (1992), the SC held that judicial review is impermissible before the Speaker passes an order, except under grave interim circumstances.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) ruled that Speakers must decide disqualification petitions within a reasonable period, usually 3 months. Law Commission and Dinesh Goswami Committee recommend vesting the power of disqualification in the Governor/President acting on the binding advice of the Election Commission.
