mcqs.q:
Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other ECs Act 2023, who constitutes the Selection Committee?
1. Prime Minister
2. Chief Justice of India
3. Leader of Opposition or single largest opposition party leader in Lok Sabha
4. A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM
Select the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: The selection committee consists of the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM, and the Leader of Opposition/single largest opposition party leader. The CJI was excluded.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of Election Commissioners under Article 324(5):
1. The CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. Any other Election Commissioner can be removed from office on the recommendation of the CEC.
3. Both CEC and ECs enjoy equal constitutional protection against arbitrary removal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect. Only the CEC enjoys the tenure protection equivalent to a Supreme Court judge. Other ECs can be removed on the recommendation of the CEC.

mcqs.q:
In which landmark judgment did a Constitution Bench direct the inclusion of the CJI in the EC selection panel until Parliament enacted a law?
(a) T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995)
(b) Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023)
(c) S.S. Dhanoa v. Union of India (1991)
(d) Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978)
options: (a) T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995)
(b) Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023)
(c) S.S. Dhanoa v. Union of India (1991)
mcqs.explanation: In Anoop Baranwal (March 2023), the 5-judge bench ordered a committee of PM, CJI, and LoP until Parliament legislated on Article 324(2).

mcqs.q:
What is the Search Committee structure established under the new Act?
(a) Headed by Cabinet Secretary with two experts
(b) Headed by Home Minister
(c) Headed by Law Minister with two other members
(d) Headed by UPSC Chairman
options: (a) Headed by Cabinet Secretary with two experts
(c) Headed by Law Minister with two other members
mcqs.explanation: The Search Committee is headed by the Minister of Law and Justice and includes two other members not below the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Chief Election Commissioner & Other ECs (Appointment & Conditions":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.

(c) 52nd Amendment Act 1985
(d) 91st Amendment Act 2003
mcqs.explanation: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 introduced the Tenth Schedule to curb political defections.

mcqs.q:
In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992), what did the Supreme Court hold regarding the Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule?
(a) Completely immune from judicial review
(b) Subject to judicial review only after the Speaker makes a final order
(c) Courts can intervene at the interlocutory stage before the Speaker decides
(d) The Speaker's role is merely administrative
options: (b) Subject to judicial review only after the Speaker makes a final order

(d) The Speaker's role is merely administrative
mcqs.explanation: The SC held that the Speaker functions as a Tribunal, and judicial review is available after a final decision on grounds of mala fide, perversity, or breach of natural justice.

(b) Protection for split by one-third of the legislature party members

(d) Exemption for the Speaker upon resigning party affiliation

(b) Protection for split by one-third of the legislature party members
(c) Disqualification on voting against party whip
(d) Exemption for the Speaker upon resigning party affiliation
mcqs.explanation: The 91st Amendment deleted Paragraph 3 of the Tenth Schedule, which had previously protected splits involving one-third members from disqualification.

mcqs.q:
A nominated member of a House becomes disqualified from membership under the Tenth Schedule if:
(a) They join a political party within six months of taking their seat
(b) They join a political party after the expiry of six months from taking their seat
(c) They do not join any political party
(d) They vote against the ruling coalition
options: (a) They join a political party within six months of taking their seat
(b) They join a political party after the expiry of six months from taking their seat
(c) They do not join any political party
(d) They vote against the ruling coalition
mcqs.explanation: Under Para 2(3) of the Tenth Schedule, a nominated member is disqualified if they join any political party after the expiry of six months from taking their seat.

The term 'Data Principal' under the DPDP Act 2023 refers to:

(b) The individual to whom the personal data relates
(c) The telecom service provider
(d) The Data Protection Officer
options: (a) The entity determining the purpose of data processing
(b) The individual to whom the personal data relates
mcqs.explanation: The DPDP Act defines 'Data Principal' as the individual to whom the personal data relates (and includes parents/legal guardians for children).

mcqs.q:
In K.S. Puttaswamy (2017), the Supreme Court ruled that the Right to Privacy is protected under which Article of the Constitution?
(a) Article 14
(b) Article 19
(c) Article 21
(d) Article 32
mcqs.explanation: The 9-judge bench unanimously held that privacy is a fundamental right emanating primarily from Article 21 (life and personal liberty) and Part III freedoms.

mcqs.q:
What is the maximum monetary penalty prescribed under the DPDP Act 2023 for significant data breach failures?
(a) Rs 50 crore
(b) Rs 100 crore
(c) Rs 250 crore
(d) Rs 500 crore
mcqs.explanation: The Act prescribes penalties up to Rs 250 crore for failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 & Rules Framewor", consider the following statements:

2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

title: National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC): Powers under Article 338B
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Rapid technological convergence in deep tech, indigenization under the National Deep Tech Startup Policy, space sector commercialization through IN-SPACe, and frontier bio-manufacturing under the BioE3 policy.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 51A(h) directs every citizen to develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry. Governed administratively by the Indian Space Policy 2023, IT Act 2000, and National Quantum Mission guidelines.

title: Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024: Central Waqf Council & Survey Commissioner
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 was introduced to revamp the administration of over 8.7 lakh registered waqf properties across India following long-standing complaints of mismanagement, arbitrary declarations under Section 40, and lack of transparency in State Waqf Boards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed by the Waqf Act 1995. Key constitutional interfaces include Article 26 (Freedom to manage religious affairs), Article 14 (Equality before law), and Article 300A (Right to property). The amendment seeks to omit Section 40 which gave boards sole authority to declare any property as waqf.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Administered by the Ministry of Minority Affairs. The Central Waqf Council (advisory body chaired by Union Minister) and State Waqf Boards oversee local mutawallis (custodians). The Bill proposes mandatory inclusion of non-Muslim members and Muslim women in both bodies.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Waqf boards collectively hold approximately 9.4 lakh acres of land valued at over ₹1.2 lakh crore, making Waqf the third-largest landholder in India after the Armed Forces and Indian Railways.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Opposition states and Muslim bodies argue that omitting Section 40 and appointing non-Muslim members infringes on denominational autonomy protected under Article 26, while the Union emphasizes preventing usurpation of government and private lands.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Sachar Committee (2006) had recommended digitizing all waqf properties and establishing Waqf Development Corporations. The Bill mandates registration on a centralized portal and survey by District Collectors instead of Survey Commissioners.

title: Delimitation of Parliamentary Constituencies: Constitutional Bar until Post-2026
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

(b) CJI + 3 senior-most judges

title: Parliamentary Privileges & Bribery Immunity: Supreme Court Verdict in Sita Soren Case
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

(d) Raja Ram Pal v. Hon'ble Speaker (2007)

(d) Raja Ram Pal v. Hon'ble Speaker (2007)

(d) When the Speaker gives sanction for prosecution

title: Inter-State River Water Disputes: Article 262 & Tribunal Adjudication Architecture
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Cauvery river water sharing conflict traces back to agreements of 1892 and 1924 between Madras Presidency and Mysore Princely State, resurfacing periodically during deficient monsoon years between Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 262 empowers Parliament to adjudicate inter-state river water disputes and bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Parliament enacted the Inter-State River Water Disputes (ISRWD) Act 1956 and River Boards Act 1956.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Administered by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Operational regulation is overseen by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), constituted under Supreme Court orders in 2018.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: In the 2018 Supreme Court judgment, Tamil Nadu was allocated 404.25 tmcft, Karnataka 284.75 tmcft, Kerala 30 tmcft, and Puducherry 7 tmcft, with 10 tmcft reserved for environmental protection and 4 tmcft for natural escape.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: The Mekedatu reservoir proposal by Karnataka and intra-state river-linking projects (Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar by Tamil Nadu) trigger repeated Special Leave Petitions (SLPs) under Article 136, bypassing Article 262's exclusion bar.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Inter-State River Water Disputes (Amendment) Bill proposes a single permanent Inter-State River Water Disputes Tribunal with multiple benches and a Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC) for mandatory pre-tribunal mediation within 1 year.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

six_point_gist.1_genesis: Genesis & Policy Background: Judicial interpretations on personal liberty, pretrial detention under special statutes (PMLA, UAPA), delays in trial, and the constitutional duty of constitutional courts under Article 32 and 226 to protect against executive arbitrariness.
six_point_gist.2_constitutional_statutory: Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty), Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention), Article 136 (Special leave to appeal), and Article 142 (Power to do complete justice). Regulated procedurally by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / CrPC 1973.
six_point_gist.3_nodal_authorities: Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Supreme Court of India, State High Courts, and Subordinate Judiciary under Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution. Nodal administrative ministry is the Ministry of Law and Justice.
six_point_gist.4_data_rankings: Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Over 5 crore cases are currently pending across Indian courts, with undertrials comprising over 75% of the total prison population according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Prison Statistics India report.
six_point_gist.5_bottlenecks_challenges: Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Stringent twin conditions for bail under Section 45 of PMLA and Section 43D(5) of UAPA, where courts must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty before granting bail, creating de facto prolonged imprisonment.
six_point_gist.6_roadmap_prelims_anchor: Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: The Supreme Court in landmark verdicts (Babu Singh, Arnesh Kumar, Manish Sisodia) has reiterated that 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception', establishing that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21.

Statutory rules: Prisons is a State subject under Entry 4 of List II (State List) in the Seventh Schedule.

digestible_fact_sheet.trap_alert: UPSC Trap Alert: Parole is an executive suspension of sentence granted by the State Government under State Prison Rules, whereas Furlough is granted as a matter of right for long-term convicts without specific cause. Neither is an inherent judicial right.

title: RBI Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) vs Reverse Repo & Liquidity Management
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.
gs_connection: Directly anchors into GS-3 Indian Economy: Monetary Policy Framework, RBI LAF Corridor (MSF - Repo - SDF), Banking Liquidity, and Money Multiplier.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) introduced by the Reserve Bank of India, consider the following statements:
1. Under the SDF, eligible commercial banks can place uncollateralised deposits with the RBI overnight.
2. The SDF rate is set 25 basis points above the Policy Repo Rate.
3. The deposits accepted by the RBI under SDF are eligible for maintenance of Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) by banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: SDF is completely uncollateralized. Statement 2 is incorrect: SDF is 25 bps BELOW the repo rate (floor of corridor; MSF is 25 bps above repo rate, acting as ceiling). Statement 3 is incorrect: Deposits under SDF are eligible for SLR, not CRR.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor of the RBI:
1. The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate acts as the upper bound (ceiling) of the corridor.
2. The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate acts as the lower bound (floor) of the corridor.
3. The width of the LAF corridor is symmetric around the Policy Repo Rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The policy repo rate sits in the middle; MSF is Repo + 25 bps (ceiling); SDF is Repo - 25 bps (floor). The corridor width is a symmetric 50 basis points.

Why was the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) recommended by the Urjit Patel Committee (2014) in place of traditional Reverse Repo?
(a) Because Reverse Repo requires RBI to transfer cash to commercial banks
(b) Because absorbing massive surplus liquidity via Reverse Repo exhausted RBI's stock of sovereign collateral (G-Secs)
(c) Because commercial banks refused to earn interest on excess reserves
(d) Because SDF increases the fiscal deficit of the Union Government
options: (a) Because Reverse Repo requires RBI to transfer cash to commercial banks
(b) Because absorbing massive surplus liquidity via Reverse Repo exhausted RBI's stock of sovereign collateral (G-Secs)
(c) Because commercial banks refused to earn interest on excess reserves
(d) Because SDF increases the fiscal deficit of the Union Government
mcqs.explanation: Traditional reverse repo requires RBI to pledge government securities as collateral. In times of extreme liquidity glut (e.g. demonetisation or heavy forex purchases), RBI ran out of G-Secs. SDF solved this collateral constraint.

mcqs.q:
When the Reserve Bank of India increases the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), what is the direct impact on the economy?
(a) Bank lending capacity expands and interest rates fall
(b) Money multiplier increases significantly
(c) Commercial banks have less loanable funds, contracting credit and liquidity
(d) Foreign direct investment automatically surges
options: (a) Bank lending capacity expands and interest rates fall
(c) Commercial banks have less loanable funds, contracting credit and liquidity
mcqs.explanation: Increasing CRR forces banks to park a higher percentage of their Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) as idle cash with RBI without interest. This reduces loanable funds, tightening liquidity and increasing borrowing costs.

(a) e₹-R is issued on blockchain while e₹-W is issued on magnetic tapes
(b) e₹-R is for public consumer transactions, while e₹-W is restricted to financial institutions for interbank settlement and secondary G-Sec transactions
(c) e₹-R carries sovereign guarantee while e₹-W is guaranteed by SEBI
(d) e₹-R is legal tender only inside India while e₹-W is used exclusively for IMF quota payments
options: (a) e₹-R is issued on blockchain while e₹-W is issued on magnetic tapes
(b) e₹-R is for public consumer transactions, while e₹-W is restricted to financial institutions for interbank settlement and secondary G-Sec transactions

mcqs.q:

3. It operates RuPay, Immediate Payment Service (IMPS), and Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. NPCI was established under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 by RBI and IBA as a non-profit company and manages India's major retail payment systems.

mcqs.q:
Which of the following enables UPI Lite to process micro-transactions without internet connectivity or PIN authentication?
(a) Cloud computing nodes at telecom towers
(b) On-device local wallet with maximum single transaction limit of ₹500
(c) Direct debit from the user's Provident Fund account
(d) Facial recognition cameras installed at retail counters

(b) On-device local wallet with maximum single transaction limit of ₹500
(c) Direct debit from the user's Provident Fund account
(d) Facial recognition cameras installed at retail counters
mcqs.explanation: UPI Lite processes low-value transactions (up to ₹500 per transaction, cumulative limit ₹2000) directly from an on-device balance without pinging the core banking system or requiring a UPI PIN, reducing bank server loads.

mcqs.q:

title: Indian Carbon Market (ICM) & Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'Indian Carbon Market (ICM) & Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (C' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.

(d) Chairman, SEBI
options: (a) Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CIRP Timelines
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The Reserve Bank of India continuously calibrates monetary instruments, retail liquidity mechanisms (e.g. RBI Retail Direct), and macroprudential measures to balance CPI inflation targets with sustained capital formation.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949. Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework was statutory enacted in 2016 through Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members (3 from RBI including Governor with casting vote, and 3 external members appointed by Central Government for a 4-year non-renewable term).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Primary inflation mandate targets Consumer Price Index (CPI) combined headline inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%). Failure is defined as missing the band for three consecutive quarters.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Transmission delays from repo rate adjustments to commercial bank lending/deposit rates, persistent food supply shocks (cereals, vegetables), and balancing exchange rate volatility against US Federal Reserve actions.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Integration of retail investors into government securities (G-Secs) through primary dealer and broker mobile applications, expansion of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee), and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) absorbing liquidity without collateral.
gs_connection: GS-3: Banking, NPAs, Ease of Doing Business, Corporate Governance, Twin Balance Sheet Problem.

mcqs.q:
What is the mandatory overall time limit prescribed under the IBC for completing the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), including legal litigation extensions?
(a) 180 days
(b) 270 days
(c) 330 days
(d) 365 days
mcqs.explanation: The 2019 amendment added a second proviso to Section 12 specifying that CIRP must mandatorily be completed within 330 days, including time taken in legal proceedings.

mcqs.q:
What voting majority in the Committee of Creditors (CoC) is required to approve a corporate resolution plan under the IBC?
(a) 51%
(b) 66%
(c) 75%
(d) Unanimous (100%)
mcqs.explanation: Under Section 30(4), a resolution plan must be approved by a vote of not less than 66% of voting share of the financial creditors.

mcqs.q:
Who acts as the Adjudicating Authority for corporate insolvency and bankruptcy under the IBC 2016?
(a) Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT)
(b) National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
(c) High Court
(d) Commercial Courts
mcqs.explanation: The NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate persons and LLPs; DRT is the adjudicating authority for individuals and partnership firms.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pre-packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP):
1. It is currently available exclusively to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
2. During the process, the existing management retains control of the company (debtor-in-possession).
3. It does not require any approval from the NCLT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect. PPIRP requires formal filing and final approval by the NCLT to have legal binding force on all stakeholders.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CI", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CI", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CI", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CI", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC): Pre-Packaged Framework & CI":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

The Unified Lending Interface (ULI) launched by the RBI is designed primarily to:
(a) Regulate international cryptocurrency transfers
(b) Enable seamless, consent-based digital flow of credit-related data to reduce loan processing time
(c) Replace credit rating agencies like CRISIL
(d) Auction sovereign treasury bills to retail participants
options: (b) Enable seamless, consent-based digital flow of credit-related data to reduce loan processing time
(c) Replace credit rating agencies like CRISIL
(d) Auction sovereign treasury bills to retail participants
mcqs.explanation: ULI is a digital public infrastructure that allows plug-and-play consent-based data access (land records, account aggregator data, GST data) to speed up credit evaluation.

mcqs.q:
The Unified Lending Interface (ULI) was developed under the aegis of which specialized subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India?
(a) Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
(b) Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH)
(c) National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
(d) Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran (BRBNMPL)
options: (a) Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
mcqs.explanation: ULI was piloted as the Public Tech Platform for Frictionless Credit (PTPFC) developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH).

mcqs.q:
Which component of Digital Public Infrastructure enables customers to share their financial data across regulated entities in a secure, consent-driven manner?
(a) Fastag Network
(b) Account Aggregator (AA) framework
(c) NEFT Protocol
(d) Bharat BillPay
mcqs.explanation: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework is an RBI-regulated non-banking financial company enabling granular, consent-based financial data sharing.

mcqs.q:
What is the primary target group benefiting from frictionless credit assessment via ULI?
(a) Large corporate conglomerates
(b) Small and marginal farmers and MSMEs with informal credit histories
(c) Foreign Institutional Investors
(d) Central Public Sector Enterprises
options: (b) Small and marginal farmers and MSMEs with informal credit histories
mcqs.explanation: ULI reduces loan processing times from weeks to minutes, directly benefiting rural borrowers and MSMEs who lack conventional collateral documentation.

title: Abolition of 'Angel Tax' (Section 56(2)(viib)) & Startup Financing
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'Abolition of 'Angel Tax' (Section 56(2)(viib)) & Startup Fin' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.
gs_connection: GS-3: Mobilization of Resources, Startup Ecosystem, Taxation Policy, Venture Capital Investments.

mcqs.q:
The term 'Angel Tax' in India specifically referred to the tax levied under which Section of the Income Tax Act, 1961?
(a) Section 10(23C)
(b) Section 56(2)(viib)
(c) Section 80C
(d) Section 115BAA
mcqs.explanation: Section 56(2)(viib) was introduced in 2012 as an anti-money laundering provision, treating excess premium on share issuance over FMV as taxable income.

mcqs.q:
Why was Angel Tax originally introduced in the Union Budget 2012?
(a) To encourage high net-worth individuals to invest in startups
(b) To curb money laundering through high-premium investment in closely held unlisted companies
(c) To tax dividends paid by tech companies
(d) To replace the Securities Transaction Tax
options: (a) To encourage high net-worth individuals to invest in startups
(b) To curb money laundering through high-premium investment in closely held unlisted companies
(c) To tax dividends paid by tech companies
(d) To replace the Securities Transaction Tax
mcqs.explanation: It was enacted to prevent laundering of unaccounted funds by routing money into unlisted companies through artificially inflated share premiums.

mcqs.q:
An 'Angel Investor' is defined as:
(a) A venture capital institution backed by the World Bank
(b) An affluent individual who provides capital for a business startup, usually in exchange for convertible debt or ownership equity
(c) A commercial bank lending under priority sector quotas
(d) A sovereign wealth fund manager
options: (a) A venture capital institution backed by the World Bank
(b) An affluent individual who provides capital for a business startup, usually in exchange for convertible debt or ownership equity
(c) A commercial bank lending under priority sector quotas
mcqs.explanation: Angel investors are high-net-worth individuals providing early-stage seed capital when formal venture funds consider risk too high.

mcqs.q:
Which nodal government department coordinates the 'Startup India' initiative and maintains the DPIIT startup recognition registry?
(a) Department of Economic Affairs
(b) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
(c) Department of Revenue
(d) Department of Financial Services
options: (b) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
mcqs.explanation: DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry is the nodal department for Startup India recognition and policy.

title: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 Sectors
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

mcqs.q:
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides cash incentives based on:
(a) Capital invested in purchasing land
(b) Incremental sales of goods manufactured in domestic units over the base year
(c) Total number of employees hired
(d) Volume of imports substituted
options: (b) Incremental sales of goods manufactured in domestic units over the base year
mcqs.explanation: PLI directly ties incentives to incremental sales of domestically manufactured goods, rewarding actual production scale rather than initial expenditure.

mcqs.q:
Which of the following sectors is covered under the 14 Champion Sectors of the PLI Scheme?
1. Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery
2. Electronic/Technology Products & Mobile Manufacturing
3. High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules
4. Coal mining equipment
Select the correct answer:
mcqs.explanation: ACC batteries, mobile/electronics, and solar PV modules are champion PLI sectors; traditional coal mining equipment is not included.

mcqs.q:
What is the primary economic objective of the PLI scheme in relation to global supply chains?
(a) To impose prohibitive import tariffs on all foreign components
(b) To integrate domestic manufacturing into Global Value Chains (GVCs) and reduce import dependencies
(c) To completely nationalize key consumer manufacturing industries
(d) To restrict exports to neighboring economies
options: (a) To impose prohibitive import tariffs on all foreign components
(b) To integrate domestic manufacturing into Global Value Chains (GVCs) and reduce import dependencies
(c) To completely nationalize key consumer manufacturing industries
(d) To restrict exports to neighboring economies
mcqs.explanation: The core objective is building domestic scale, plugging into global value chains, and generating export surplus while lowering supply vulnerability.

mcqs.q:
Which sector was the pioneer and demonstrated the highest early disbursement under the PLI initiative?
(a) Textile manufacturing
(b) Large-Scale Electronics and Mobile Manufacturing
(c) Specialty Steel
(d) White Goods (ACs and LEDs)
mcqs.explanation: Large-Scale Electronics and Mobile manufacturing showed rapid scale, making India a net exporter of smartphones within 3 years.

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 S", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 S", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 S", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 S", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Assessment across 14 S":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

(b) 100% tax holiday for any 10 consecutive years out of a block of 15 years

(d) Full exemption from import customs duties on raw materials only

mcqs.q:
The term 'Deemed Foreign Territory' in the context of GIFT City IFSC implies that:
(a) Indian criminal laws do not apply
(b) Transactions are treated as offshore foreign exchange transactions for exchange control purposes
(c) Only foreign citizens can work in the jurisdiction
(d) India does not possess territorial sovereignty over the zone

(b) Transactions are treated as offshore foreign exchange transactions for exchange control purposes
(c) Only foreign citizens can work in the jurisdiction
(d) India does not possess territorial sovereignty over the zone

mcqs.q:
Which exchange in GIFT City launched trading in SGX Nifty derivatives, renaming it GIFT Nifty?
(a) National Stock Exchange IFSC (NSE IX)

(d) Metropolitan Stock Exchange
mcqs.explanation: GIFT Nifty trades on NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) within GIFT City, repatriating offshore dollar trading from Singapore to India.

mcqs.q:
The Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework differs from the traditional provisioning model primarily because:
(a) It relies solely on government guarantees
(b) It requires banks to estimate future credit defaults prospectively rather than waiting for an actual default to occur
(c) It eliminates the concept of Non-Performing Assets completely
(d) It applies only to retail personal loans
options: (a) It relies solely on government guarantees
(b) It requires banks to estimate future credit defaults prospectively rather than waiting for an actual default to occur
(c) It eliminates the concept of Non-Performing Assets completely
(d) It applies only to retail personal loans
mcqs.explanation: ECL is forward-looking and requires provisioning based on economic cycles and early credit distress signals rather than post-facto default.

mcqs.q:
Under the ECL approach aligned with IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109, what does Stage 2 classification signify?
(a) Zero risk of default
(b) Significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, requiring lifetime expected loss provisioning
(c) Actual default / credit-impaired asset
(d) Sovereign debt asset
options: (b) Significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, requiring lifetime expected loss provisioning
mcqs.explanation: Stage 2 represents financial instruments with significant increase in credit risk since origination, requiring lifetime expected credit loss recognition.

mcqs.q:
Which international regulatory framework established the foundation for Expected Credit Loss provisioning following the 2008 global financial crisis?
(a) Basel I
(b) Basel II
(c) Basel III
(d) Bretton Woods Agreement
mcqs.explanation: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) under Basel III reforms mandated ECL models to resolve the procyclicality of incurred loss models.

mcqs.q:
What is the standard regulatory criteria for an asset to be classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) in Indian commercial banks?
(a) Interest or principal overdue for more than 30 days
(b) Interest or principal overdue for more than 60 days
(c) Interest or principal overdue for more than 90 days
(d) Overdue for more than 180 days
options: (a) Interest or principal overdue for more than 30 days
(b) Interest or principal overdue for more than 60 days
(c) Interest or principal overdue for more than 90 days
mcqs.explanation: Under RBI prudential norms, a loan asset is classified as an NPA if interest or installment of principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.

title: India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: The developments surrounding 'India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone' represent a strategic policy evolution addressing national regulatory oversight, institutional accountability, and socioeconomic service delivery under modern public administration standards.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Anchored within the constitutional framework of Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), and statutory authority exercised under Parliamentary enactments ensuring rule of law and procedural due process.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Coordinated by the concerned Union Ministries and Statutory Regulatory Authorities with institutional mandates to establish uniform national standards, conduct periodic audits, and enforce statutory compliance.

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Backed by targeted fiscal allocations under Central Sector or Centrally Sponsored Schemes, tracked through digital governance portals (DBT, PRAGATI) to reduce implementation leakages and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Primary administrative hurdles involve centre-state cooperative federalism challenges, inter-departmental coordination deficits, compliance burdens on grassroots stakeholders, and judicial oversight of executive discretion.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: NITI Aayog recommendations emphasize evidence-based policymaking, digital public infrastructure integration, outcome-based budgeting, and strengthening statutory dispute resolution mechanisms.
gs_connection: GS-3: External Sector, Balance of Payments, Forex Management, RBI Balance Sheet, Currency Stability.

mcqs.q:
Which of the following is NOT a component of India's Foreign Exchange Reserves?
(a) Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)
(b) Gold holdings of the RBI
(c) Special Drawing Rights (SDR) with the IMF
(d) Indian Corporate Rupee Bonds held by domestic mutual funds
options: (c) Special Drawing Rights (SDR) with the IMF
(d) Indian Corporate Rupee Bonds held by domestic mutual funds
mcqs.explanation: Forex reserves comprise 4 components: Foreign Currency Assets, Gold, SDRs, and Reserve Position in the IMF (RTP).

mcqs.q:
The 'Reserve Tranche Position' (RTP) in the International Monetary Fund refers to:
(a) The gold deposited by developing nations as penalty
(b) The portion of a member country's quota paid in reserve currencies that can be withdrawn on demand without conditionality
(c) The emergency loan extended to member countries under Structural Adjustment Programs
(d) The interest charged on SDR allocations
options: (a) The gold deposited by developing nations as penalty
(b) The portion of a member country's quota paid in reserve currencies that can be withdrawn on demand without conditionality
(c) The emergency loan extended to member countries under Structural Adjustment Programs
(d) The interest charged on SDR allocations
mcqs.explanation: A member country's quota with the IMF includes the Reserve Tranche, which is an unconditional reserve asset that can be drawn without policy obligations.

mcqs.q:
What is the primary currency basket determining the value of the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR)?
(a) US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, British Pound
(b) US Dollar, Euro, Indian Rupee, Russian Rouble
(c) US Dollar and Euro only
(d) Gold, Silver, and Platinum bullion prices
options: (a) US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, British Pound
(b) US Dollar, Euro, Indian Rupee, Russian Rouble
(d) Gold, Silver, and Platinum bullion prices
mcqs.explanation: The SDR basket consists of five currencies: US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Yuan/Renminbi (added in 2016), Japanese Yen, and British Pound Sterling.

mcqs.q:
What is the economic concept of 'Import Cover' of forex reserves?
(a) The custom duty levied on imported luxury items
(b) The number of months of imports that can be sustained by a country's foreign currency reserves
(c) The insurance policy covering marine transport shipments
(d) The ratio of exports to total imports
options: (a) The custom duty levied on imported luxury items
(b) The number of months of imports that can be sustained by a country's foreign currency reserves
(c) The insurance policy covering marine transport shipments
(d) The ratio of exports to total imports
mcqs.explanation: Import cover measures how many months a nation can finance its projected import bill using its foreign exchange reserves (safe benchmark is 8-10 months).

mcqs.q:
With reference to the institutional mechanisms concerning "India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone", consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body derives its powers from an Act of Parliament, whereas an executive body is established via a Cabinet resolution.
2. Decisions of a statutory regulatory authority cannot be challenged in High Courts under writ jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory bodies (like SEBI, CPCB, NHRC) are established by Acts of Parliament, while executive bodies (like NITI Aayog) are set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is incorrect: Decisions of statutory authorities are subject to judicial review under Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q:
In the context of Indian constitutional governance relevant to "India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone", consider the following statements:
1. The power of judicial review of legislative enactments and executive actions is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. Article 142 grants plenary powers to the apex court to ensure complete justice between parties.

mcqs.q:
Regarding statutory administrative frameworks associated with "India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone", consider the following statements:
1. Subordinate legislation (rules and regulations) framed by executive ministries must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
2. A statutory body has the inherent power to override explicit provisions of the parent statute under which it was constituted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Delegated legislation must be laid before Parliament and is scrutinized by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation of both Houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Subordinate or statutory bodies cannot exceed or override the scope of their parent enactment (doctrine of ultra vires).

mcqs.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding institutional authorities and their parent Union Ministries:
1. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) : Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) : Ministry of Jal Shakti
3. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

mcqs.q:
With reference to India's international obligations in policy domains linked to "India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone", consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 253 of the Constitution, Parliament has exclusive power to make any law for implementing any treaty or convention, even on subjects enumerated in the State List.
2. Treaties signed and ratified by the Government of India automatically become part of domestic law without requiring any implementing parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements. Statement 2 is incorrect: India follows a 'dualist' model of international law; international treaties do not automatically become enforceable in domestic courts without an enabling statute passed by Parliament.

mcqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regulatory and constitutional boundary conditions related to "India's Foreign Exchange Reserves & Import Cover Milestone":
1. All regulatory notifications issued by central statutory commissions require prior approval of the President of India before taking effect.
2. The Constitution mandates that the Union Government cannot issue executive directions to States on matters where both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false: Statutory commissions issue gazette notifications under delegated powers without requiring individual presidential approval. Statement 2 is false: Under Article 256 and Article 73(1) proviso, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament on concurrent subjects.

title: Internationalisation of the Rupee: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA)
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: India's active multi-alignment foreign policy balancing strategic autonomy, leadership of the Global South (Voice of Global South Summit), maritime domain security in the Indo-Pacific, and navigation of supply chain resilience initiatives.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 51 (DPSP: Promotion of international peace and security) and Article 253 (Parliament's power to legislate for giving effect to international treaties and agreements even on State List subjects).

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS), and representation in multilateral groupings (G20, BRICS, SCO, Quad, BIMSTEC, Colombo Security Conclave).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: Expanded BRICS now accounts for approximately 45% of the world population and 28% of global nominal GDP, while IMEC corridor aims to cut transit time between India and Europe by 40% and logistics costs by 30%.

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: Geopolitical instability across maritime chokepoints (Bab-el-Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz), divergent positions on Ukraine/Middle East conflicts, trade barriers, and negotiating bilateral investment treaties under India's 2016 Model BIT.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Deepening maritime domain awareness through the Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (IPMDA) and the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS), combined with bilateral trade settlement in local currencies.

(c) Mutual escrow account
(d) Sovereign foreign exchange account
mcqs.explanation: Vostro means 'your account with us' (a foreign bank's account maintained at an Indian bank in INR). Nostro means 'our account with you' (an Indian bank's account maintained abroad in foreign currency).

mcqs.q:
Under RBI's rupee trade settlement mechanism, how can a foreign exporter be paid for goods shipped to India?
(a) Through physical currency notes only
(b) Indian importer pays in INR, which is credited to the foreign bank's Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA) in India
(c) Payment must be cleared through New York CHIPS system in USD
(d) Via barter arrangement of gold bullion
options: (b) Indian importer pays in INR, which is credited to the foreign bank's Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA) in India
(c) Payment must be cleared through New York CHIPS system in USD
(d) Via barter arrangement of gold bullion
mcqs.explanation: The Indian importer pays in Indian Rupees, which is credited into the Special Vostro account of the correspondent bank of the partner country.

mcqs.q:

(b) Urjit Patel Committee
(c) Bimal Jalan Committee
(d) Rangarajan Committee
mcqs.explanation: The Tarapore Committees on Capital Account Convertibility (1997 and 2006) laid down preconditions including low fiscal deficit, low inflation, and robust banking health.

(a) Elimination of exchange rate volatility and dependency on the US Dollar clearing system
(b) Complete isolation from global inflation trends

(d) Exemption from WTO tariff bindings
options: (a) Elimination of exchange rate volatility and dependency on the US Dollar clearing system
(b) Complete isolation from global inflation trends
(c) Guaranteed surplus on the current account

1. Merchandise trade (exports and imports)
2. Software services receipts
3. Remittances by non-resident Indians
4. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)
Select the correct answer:
mcqs.explanation: FDI, FPI, and external commercial borrowings belong to the Capital Account. Trade in goods, services, income, and unilateral transfers (remittances) form the Current Account.

mcqs.q:
In balance of payments accounting, 'Invisibles' comprise:
(a) Smuggled contraband goods
(b) Services, transfers (remittances/grants), and factor income (interest/dividends)
(c) Defense capital expenditure
(d) Trade conducted through darknet platforms
mcqs.explanation: Invisibles in the current account consist of non-merchandise transactions: services (IT, travel, transport), transfers (gifts, remittances), and income flows.

mcqs.q:
According to the World Bank's Migration and Development Brief, which country is the world's top recipient of external remittances?
(a) China
(b) Mexico
(c) India
(d) Philippines
mcqs.explanation: India is the world's largest recipient of remittances, surpassing $120 billion annually, with substantial flows from North America, UK, and the Gulf.

A country running a persistent Current Account Deficit must finance it through:
(a) An equivalent surplus on its Capital Account or drawing down forex reserves
(b) Printing fiat currency exclusively
(c) Imposing domestic export bans
(d) Increasing domestic statutory minimum wages
options: (a) An equivalent surplus on its Capital Account or drawing down forex reserves
mcqs.explanation: By BoP identity (Current Account + Capital Account + Changes in Reserves = 0), a CAD must be financed by capital inflows (FDI/FPI/loans) or by drawing down reserves.

title: Minimum Support Price (MSP) Formulas: Swaminathan Commission & C2 vs A2+FL
summary_points: Genesis & Policy Background: Rapid technological convergence in deep tech, indigenization under the National Deep Tech Startup Policy, space sector commercialization through IN-SPACe, and frontier bio-manufacturing under the BioE3 policy.

Constitutional & Statutory Architecture: Article 51A(h) directs every citizen to develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry. Governed administratively by the Indian Space Policy 2023, IT Act 2000, and National Quantum Mission guidelines.

Nodal Authorities & Institutional Governance: Department of Space (ISRO, IN-SPACe, NewSpace India Limited - NSIL), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and Department of Science and Technology (DST).

Critical Quantitative Metrics & Fiscal Indicators: India's R&D expenditure stands at approximately 0.65% of GDP, with targets to increase to 2%. National Quantum Mission was approved with an outlay of ₹6,003 crore over 8 years (2023-2031).

Key Bottlenecks, Challenges & Federal/Legal Friction: High import reliance on advanced semiconductor fabrication (sub-7nm), intellectual property licensing bottlenecks, private sector R&D expenditure deficits, and cross-border data transfer compliance under DPDP Act 2023.

Strategic Roadmap & Prelims High-Yield Takeaway: Commercialization through NSIL (commercial arm of ISRO) and IN-SPACe (single-window nodal agency for non-government private entities), Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act 2023 mobilizing ₹50,000 crore for university research.

mcqs.q:
Which statutory/advisory body recommends the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) to the Central Government?
(a) NITI Aayog
(b) Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
(c) National Farmers Commission
(d) Food Corporation of India
options: (b) Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
mcqs.explanation: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture, recommends MSPs. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approves them.

mcqs.q:
In agricultural cost terminology used by CACP, what does 'A2+FL' cost include?
(a) Only seeds and chemical fertilizers
(b) All paid-out costs on inputs, hired labor, fuels, irrigation plus the imputed value of unpaid family labor
(c) Comprehensive cost including rental value of owned land and interest on owned capital
(d) Only the market transportation charges to mandis
options: (b) All paid-out costs on inputs, hired labor, fuels, irrigation plus the imputed value of unpaid family labor
(c) Comprehensive cost including rental value of owned land and interest on owned capital
(d) Only the market transportation charges to mandis
mcqs.explanation: Cost A2 covers all paid-out expenses incurred by the farmer. A2+FL adds the imputed value of family labor. C2 is comprehensive cost (A2+FL + land rent + capital interest).

mcqs.q:
The National Commission on Farmers chaired by Prof. M.S. Swaminathan recommended that MSP should be at least:
(a) 25% above A2 cost
(b) 50% above the weighted average Cost of Production (C2)
(c) Equal to international benchmark market prices
(d) 100% above input expenditure
options: (b) 50% above the weighted average Cost of Production (C2)
(c) Equal to international benchmark market prices
mcqs.explanation: The Swaminathan Commission report (2006) famously recommended fixing MSP at least 50% more than the comprehensive cost of production (C2).

mcqs.q:
For sugarcane, instead of MSP, the Central Government announces:
(a) Minimum Export Price (MEP)
(b) Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)
(c) Statutory Maximum Retail Price
(d) Procurement Buffer Price
mcqs.explanation: Under the Sugarcane (Control) Order 1966, the Union Government fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) that sugar mills are legally obligated to pay cane growers.

mcqs.q:

mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. In Minerva Mills (1980) and L. Chandra Kumar (1997), the Supreme Court affirmed that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is an unalterable basic feature of the Constitution. (a) Outright sale and privatization of state-owned land assets
(b) Leasing brownfield, de-risked revenue-generating public infrastructure assets to private operators while retaining public ownership
(c) Shutting down non-profitable public enterprises
(d) Sovereign borrowing from foreign commercial banks
options: (a) Outright sale and privatization of state-owned land assets
(b) Leasing brownfield, de-risked revenue-generating public infrastructure assets to private operators while retaining public ownership
(d) Sovereign borrowing from foreign commercial banks

(d) Masala Bonds

(a) Greenfield involves high environmental risk, while brownfield involves low environmental risk
(b) Greenfield involves building entirely new assets from scratch; brownfield involves expanding or monetizing existing operating assets
(c) Greenfield applies only to agriculture; brownfield applies to heavy manufacturing
(d) Brownfield is exclusively financed by foreign equity
options: (a) Greenfield involves high environmental risk, while brownfield involves low environmental risk
(b) Greenfield involves building entirely new assets from scratch; brownfield involves expanding or monetizing existing operating assets
(c) Greenfield applies only to agriculture; brownfield applies to heavy manufacturing
(d) Brownfield is exclusively financed by foreign equity
mcqs.explanation: Greenfield projects carry land acquisition and construction execution risks; brownfield assets are already built, de-risked, and generating operating cash flows.

mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 253 confers overriding power on Parliament to legislate on State List entries to implement international agreements.
